## What this saves you

The "coordination-native" benchmark plans (AgentsNet, SwarmBench, …) all vendor a
third-party Python harness that picks its per-agent LLM via LangChain's
`init_chat_model(model_name, model_provider)`, and want **claude-opus-4-8 @ xhigh**
routed through our localhost inference gateway. The brief usually says "register the
gateway as an **OpenAI-compatible** MODEL_PROVIDER." That is **wrong** and will cost
you an afternoon. Here is the recipe that works (proven end-to-end on AgentsNet,
`benchmark-suite-agentsnet-2026-06-17`).

## The gateway is an Anthropic proxy, not OpenAI-compatible

`packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway.ts` only proxies `/v1/*` and
specially parses `/v1/messages` — it is the **Anthropic Messages API**. There is no
`/v1/chat/completions`. So route the LangChain client as **anthropic**, not openai:

- `MODEL_PROVIDER["claude-opus-4-8"] = "anthropic"`
- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = http://127.0.0.1:8788` (or `base_url=` kwarg to `ChatAnthropic`)
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = <anything>` — the gateway **strips** the client's auth and
  reinjects the real Claude-Max OAuth bearer + the `oauth-2025-04-20` beta. The key
  only needs to be SET.
- model id `claude-opus-4-8` (the price table prefix-resolves it; the `claude` CLI's
  "4-8 silently runs 4-7" gotcha is a CLI-alias thing — the RAW API passes the id
  verbatim, so it's correct here).

## The first system block MUST be the Claude Code identity

On a Max-OAuth token, a raw-SDK caller whose first `system` block is not **exactly**
`You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude.` (as its OWN block) gets a
**bogus 429** (`rate_limit_error`) regardless of budget — see
[max-oauth-first-system-block-must-be-claude-code-identity](/internal/docs/agent-insights/max-oauth-first-system-block-must-be-claude-code-identity).
With `langchain-anthropic`, send the system message as a **list of content blocks**
with the CC identity first:

```python
SystemMessage(content=[
    {"type": "text", "text": "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude."},
    {"type": "text", "text": <the benchmark's real system prompt>},
])
```

Tell a framing-reject from a real rate-limit: the framing reject's body is literally
`"Error"` with no `anthropic-ratelimit-*` headers; a genuine 429 carries a full
message + a `request_id` + reset headers (then it's budget, not framing).

## xhigh = extended thinking at 32k

There is no "effort" param on the raw API. `xhigh` is realized as extended thinking
at `budget_tokens=32000` (matches `external-bench/competitor-live.ts`
`DEFAULT_THINKING_BUDGET_TOKENS`), with `max_tokens > budget_tokens`
(`32000 + 16384`). **Gotcha:** with thinking on, `ChatAnthropic` returns
`AIMessage.content` as a **list of blocks** (thinking + text). If the harness's
parsers expect a string, flatten it (drop thinking/redacted_thinking, keep text) at
the single model-call chokepoint. For plain multi-turn chat (no tool_use) you do NOT
need to preserve thinking blocks across turns, so flattening is safe.

## Dodge fleet exhaustion: pin a fresh account

The shared gateway's active account is often the fleet-exhausted one (`unified 5h
utilization: 1.0, rejected: true` in `GET :8788/stats`). Pin your benchmark to a
fresh pool account with the **`x-papercusp-account: <id>`** header
(`accounts:status` shows per-account utilization; pick one at ~0%). With
`langchain-anthropic`: `default_headers={"x-papercusp-account": "<id>"}`. The gateway
selects that account (`gateway.ts` `pool.select`) and strips the header upstream.

## Resilience for overload (529)

Anthropic returns transient **529 OverloadedError** under load. Let the **Anthropic
SDK's own retry** handle it (`max_retries=8` — it honors `Retry-After` and backs off);
don't set it to 0. A long benchmark then rides out overload windows. Pace concurrency
with a client rate limiter and run each (size,task) as a separate invocation so one
bad window can't lose the whole run.

## Vendoring gotchas (Python)

- **`numpy==1.26.4`** has no wheels for py3.13/3.14 → use **py3.11** (`uv venv
  --python 3.11`, mirroring the existing bench harnesses).
- The README's pip list **omits `regex`** even though the code `import regex`s it.
- A repo written pre-langchain-1.x uses `from langchain.schema import …` /
  `langchain.prompts` — these moved to **`langchain_core.messages` /
  `langchain_core.prompts`** in 1.x. `init_chat_model` stays at `langchain.chat_models`.
- `init_chat_model(model)` will `KeyError` if the harness keys a per-model
  rate-limiter dict on the model name — add a default fallback entry.
- `langchain-anthropic` may need an explicit install even when listed (verify
  `from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic`).

Keep all this behind one env flag (e.g. `AGENTSNET_GATEWAY=1`) in a small support
module so the vendored diff stays auditable and re-vendorable.
